title: Customer FinOps QBR Workbook - Usage & Billing Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a working workbook and playbook for Customer Success to run the usage & billing section of Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs). Focus is token spend analysis, rate-limit risk, budget alerts, and renewal talking points tied to usage economics. This is intentionally lightweight so CSMs can copy into a customer-facing slide deck or a one-page summary.

How to use this doc (quick):
- Before the QBR: pull last 90/30/7 day token usage, per-route breakdown, and billing line items. Paste the numbers into the SUMMARY TABLE below.
- During QBR: walk through trends, call out anomalies and throttles, present forecast and suggested actions.
- After QBR: create tickets (JIRA/PR) for follow-ups, schedule optimization pairing with Solutions Eng if needed.

SECTION A — Executive Snapshot (one slide summary)
- Top-line: Last 90 days token spend: ${{PAST_90_DOLLARS}} (tokens: {{PAST_90_TOKENS}})
- Spend trend vs prior 90 days: +/-(%) = {{TREND_PERCENT}}
- Active routes: {{NUM_ROUTES}} (top 3: {{ROUTE_1}}, {{ROUTE_2}}, {{ROUTE_3}})
- Rate-limit risk: {{RISK_LEVEL}} (current peak RPS: {{PEAK_RPS}}, configured soft quota: {{SOFT_QPS}})
- Alerts fired this period: {{NUM_ALERTS}} (types: budget, 429-rate-limit, quota-violation)
- Renewal window: {{RENEWAL_DATE}} — recommended ask: renew with commitment of {{SUGGESTED_COMMITMENT}} to reduce unit cost by {{SUGGESTED_DISCOUNT_PCT}}%

SECTION B — Data Inputs (what we collect and where)
- Billing: raw invoice line items exported from Stripe/Billing dashboard (CSV). Fields needed: invoice_id, period_start, period_end, gross_amount, credits, net_amount, billing_units (tokens/embeddings).
- Usage: API request logs grouped by route/model. Fields: timestamp, route, model_version, tokens_in, tokens_out, request_latency_ms, response_status.
- Limits: per-customer rate-limit configs from Console + any custom routing policies.
- Alerts: PagerDuty/Cloud alerts + internal budget-alert webhook history.

SECTION C — SUMMARY TABLE (copy this into your QBR slides)
- Table header: [Metric | 90-day | 30-day | 7-day | Delta (30 vs 90) | Note]
- Total tokens consumed | {{TOTAL_TOKENS_90}} | {{TOTAL_TOKENS_30}} | {{TOTAL_TOKENS_7}} | {{DELTA_TOKENS}} | e.g., heavy dev spike on 2025-02-05
- Total billed spend | ${{TOTAL_SPEND_90}} | ${{TOTAL_SPEND_30}} | ${{TOTAL_SPEND_7}} | {{DELTA_SPEND}} | includes embedding batch credits
- Gen (completion) tokens | {{GEN_TOKENS_90}} | {{GEN_TOKENS_30}} | {{GEN_TOKENS_7}} | {{DELTA_GEN}} | top route: customer-chat
- Embedding tokens | {{EMB_TOKENS_90}} | {{EMB_TOKENS_30}} | {{EMB_TOKENS_7}} | {{DELTA_EMB}} | nightly batch job is dominant
- Avg cost per 1k tokens | ${{COST_PER_1K_90}} | ... | ... | ... | compute = spend / (tokens/1000)
- Peak RPS observed | {{PEAK_RPS}} | {{PEAK_RPS_30}} | {{PEAK_RPS_7}} | - | note any 429s

SECTION D — Alerts & Incidents (recent 90-day)
- Budget alerts fired (dates):
  - 2025-01-03: budget threshold 75% hit — emailed customer + automated cap applied (no disruption)
  - 2025-02-09: sudden 50% daily spike — alert suppressed initially, later acknowledged
- Rate-limit incidents:
  - 2025-02-10: sustained 429 bursts on route /v1/chat/send — cause: consumer event loop retry storm; mitigation: apply short backoff + temporary quota bump
- Open follow-ups: ticket CS-4892 (add per-route quota granularity), SE-990 (embedding batching pilot)

SECTION E — Playbook: If spend is rising rapidly
- Step 0: Verify raw logs match billing (detect ingestion vs billing mismatch). If >5% discrepancy open Billing-Investigation ticket.
- Step 1: Identify root route(s) (top 5 by tokens). Annotate whether interactive, background, or batch.
- Step 2: For background/batch jobs: recommend batching windows, move to nighttime, increase chunk size for embeddings -> estimated token reduction: 15-40%.
- Step 3: For chat/interactive: enable prefix caching where possible; evaluate smaller model for non-critical intents; introduce partial responses (delta streaming) to reduce gen tokens.
- Step 4: Rate limit mitigation: add client-side exponential backoff + jitter; configure soft quota with email warning at 60%, hard cap at 95% of committed throughput.
- Step 5: Apply quantifiable ask in renewal: propose a committed monthly unit (tokens) with explicit overage pricing and 30-day review cadence.

SECTION F — Playbook: If customer hits consistent 429s
- Quick triage checklist:
  1) Confirm if 429s are client-side (retries) or server-side (enforcement) by sampling headers (x-rate-limit-window, x-rate-limit-remaining).
  2) Correlate 429 timestamps with deploys. New deploys can cause retry storms.
  3) If customer uses many short-lived connections (mobile), suggest connection pooling and a global soft queue on client.
  4) Temp remediation: increase soft quota for 72 hours while implementing client fixes; capture traffic patterns and plan steady-state capacity.

SECTION G — Forecast model (simple)
- Inputs: avg_daily_tokens (30d), monthly_growth_rate, planned feature launches (date & estimated delta).
- Formula (text): projected_monthly_tokens = avg_daily_tokens * 30 * (1 + monthly_growth_rate) + sum(feature_delta_tokens).
- Quick sensitivity: show 3 scenarios: conservative (0% growth), expected (customer forecast), aggressive (+50% of expected).

SECTION H — Renewal talking points tied to usage economics
- If usage stable/declining: propose multi-month renewal with lower unit price and rollback clause for usage regressions.
- If usage growing predictably: propose tiered commitment that auto-expands at negotiated unit prices; highlight savings from Reserved vs On-demand.
- If customer shows spiky traffic: recommend Dedicated burst capacity pilot + SLA add-on to reduce 429 risk.
- Sample ask language: "Based on the last 90 days your average monthly token consumption is X. We recommend a 12-month commitment at Y tokens/month which reduces the unit cost by Z% and gives you guaranteed QPS and priority routing."

SECTION I — Suggested slides/outputs to include in QBR
- Slide 1: Executive snapshot (one-line cost + trend)
- Slide 2: Usage breakdown (top 5 routes, embedding vs gen)
- Slide 3: Alerts & incidents (timeline)
- Slide 4: Forecast & scenarios (numbers)
- Slide 5: Ask & options (commitment tiers, Dedicated pilot, optimization plan)

NOTES / CAVEATS
- All token accounting is only as accurate as the ingestion pipeline. If logs are sampled, call that out.
- Embedding jobs often look expensive but they can be shifted to cheaper schedules or quantized model variants.
- Avoid promising precise $ savings until SE runs a reproducible benchmark. Use ranges.

Appendix: Useful quick checks for CSMs
- Quick SQL to get top routes by tokens (pseudocode):
  SELECT route, SUM(tokens_in + tokens_out) as tokens FROM api_logs WHERE customer_id = '{{CUST_ID}}' AND timestamp >= DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE, INTERVAL 90 DAY) GROUP BY route ORDER BY tokens DESC LIMIT 10;
- Alert rule snippets:
  - BudgetAlert: if projected_monthly_spend > monthly_budget AND day_of_month <= 5 -> send email + create task + optional cap
  - RateLimitAlert: if 429_rate > 0.5% of requests in 15m window -> page SRE on priority if > 1%

Revision history:
- 2025-02-18 initial draft by Maya Chen
- 2025-02-25 added forecast template (Ethan)
- 2025-03-12 added incident examples + playbook tweaks (Sofia)

Open questions / TODOs for CS leadership:
- Should we bake a standardized SQL + BigQuery view for per-customer token accounting?
- Who owns the default soft quota settings for new mid-market customers?
- Can we create a templated Commitment vs On-demand calculator for renewals?

End of workbook.
